WHILE THE DISCOVERY OF CALCIUM-ALUMINUM RICH INCLUSIONS AND CHONDRULE-LIKE OBJECTS IN COMET WILD 2 SHOWED THAT OUTWARD MIGRATION OF SUB-MM SIZED-PARTICLES OCCURRED VERY EARLY IN THE SOLAR SYSTEM  THE EXTENT AND DIRECTION(S) OF MIGRATION AFTER THIS EARLY TIME IN SOLAR SYSTEM HISTORY IS NOT KNOWN. THE PROPOSED WORK IS RELEVANT TO THE SCOPE OF THE EMERGING WORLDS PROGRAM  AS ITS GOAL IS   TO ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE OF THE SOLAR SYSTEM BY INVESTIGATING HOW IT FORMED AND EVOLVED  THROUGH THE ANALYSES OF EXTRATERRESTRIAL MATERIALS IN THE LABORATORY. EMERGING WORLDS IS MOST APPROPRIATE FOR THIS RESEARCH SINCE IT IS RELEVANT TO MULTIPLE TOPICS LISTED IN THE PROGRAM S SCOPE IN C.2.  INCLUDING  BUT NOT LIMITED TO:  STUDIES OF ALL ASPECTS OF MATERIALS PRESENT AND PROCESSES OCCURRING IN AND AFFECTING THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK  . WE WILL ACHIEVE THESE GOALS BY DETERMINING THE MORPHOLOGIES  ELEMENTAL  AND O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS USING STATE-OF-THE-ART COORDINATED MICROANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES (FIELD EMISSION ELECTRON PROBE MICROANALYSIS AND SECONDARY ION MASS SPECTROMETRY). PARTIALLY MELTED CHONDRULES CONTAIN UNMELTED CHONDRULE PRECURSOR SILICATES THAT SURVIVED HEATING DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION  WHICH ARE TERMED RELICT GRAINS. THESE RELICT GRAINS MAY BE PRIMORDIAL SILICATES RELATED TO REFRACTORY INCLUSIONS  RECYCLED CHONDRULE FRAGMENTS FROM THE SAME METEORITE GROUP  XENOCRYSTS FROM ANOTHER CHONDRITE GROUP  OR DEBRIS FROM DIFFERENTIATED/ UNDIFFERENTIATED PLANETESIMALS. RELICT GRAINS IN CHONDRULES ARE IMPORTANT TO STUDY BECAUSE WE KNOW THEY WERE PRESENT DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION IN THE EARLY SOLAR SYSTEM. BY CONSTRAINING THE ORIGIN(S) OF RELICT GRAINS IN CHONDRULES FROM METEORITE GROUPS WITH DISTINCT ESTABLISHED FORMATION AGES THAT FORMED AT DISTINCT RADIAL LOCATIONS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK  WE WILL INVESTIGATE GRAIN MIGRATION BETWEEN CHONDRITE GROUPS PRIOR TO AND DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION AND CONSTRAIN THEIR SOURCE(S). OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT CHONDRULE FRAGMENTS MIGRATED BETWEEN DISTINCT CHONDRULE-FORMING REGIONS  FROM THE NON-CARBONACEOUS [NC] METEORITE REGION IN THE INNER SOLAR SYSTEM TO THE CARBONACEOUS CHONDRITE [CC] METEORITE REGION IN THE OUTER SOLAR SYSTEM REGION  IMPLYING OUTWARD MIGRATION OF GRAINS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK. OUR DATA WILL HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR MIXING OF MATERIAL IN THE EARLY SOLAR SYSTEM  AND ASSUMING 26AL HOMOGENEITY  PROVIDE ESTIMATES ON THE TIMING OF SUCH MIGRATION(S) BETWEEN FORMATION REGIONS. DETERMINING THE ORIGIN(S) OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS  RELICT GRAINS  WILL PROVIDE ANALYTICAL CONSTRAINTS TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT THE RADIAL MIGRATION OF GRAINS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK DURING THE ERA OF CHONDRULE FORMATION WAS OUTWARD.

EACH SUMMER THE NORTH AMERICAN MONSOON ANTICYCLONE (NAMA) DOMINATES THE CIRCULATION OF THE NORTH-WESTERN HEMISPHERE AND ACTS TO PARTIALLY CONFINE AND ISOLATE AIR FROM THE SURROUNDING ATMOSPHERE. STRONG CONVECTIVE STORMS IN THE NAMA REGULARLY PENETRATE DEEP INTO THE LOWER STRATOSPHERE (LS), WITH SOME ASCENDING ABOVE 20 KM (~450 K POTENTIAL TEMPERATURE). THE UNIQUENESS OF THE NAMA REGION IS MOST EASILY SEEN IN SATELLITE MEASUREMENTS OF WATER VAPOR, WHICH SHOW A LARGE ENHANCEMENT IN THE LS OVER NORTH AMERICA NOT SEEN EITHER IN MAGNITUDE OR AT SUCH HIGH LATITUDES ELSEWHERE AROUND THE GLOBE. BUT THE COUPLING OF TROPOPAUSE-PENETRATING CONVECTION WITH LARGE-SCALE MONSOONAL MOTION IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD, AS IS THE IMPACT OF CONVECTION ON THE CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF THE LS, BOTH IN MONSOON REGIONS AND IN THE GLOBAL STRATOSPHERE, WHICH RECEIVES INPUTS OF MOIST AND POLLUTED MONSOON AIR FROM THE NAMA. THE DYNAMICS AND CHEMISTRY OF THE SUMMER STRATOSPHERE (DCOTSS) PROPOSAL DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP.

Award or Action Description: MOROCCO IS A DROUGHT-PRONE  CLIMATE-CONSTRAINED COUNTRY THAT HAS MADE SIGNIFICANT INVESTMENTS IN AGRICULTURE WITH THE GOAL OF ENHANCING THE ADOPTION OF HIGHER-VALUE CROPPING SYSTEMS FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. THE MOROCCAN GOVERNMENT CURRENTLY OFFERS A MULTI-PERIL INSURANCE PROGRAM FOR CEREAL CROPS BUT HAS NOT YET DEVELOPED A PRODUCT THAT COULD HELP ABSORB THE RISKS IMPEDING THE ADOPTION OF SUCH HIGHER VALUE  BUT RISKIER  CROPPING SYSTEMS. WITHIN THIS CONTEXT  TWO EARLY-CAREER SCIENTISTS WITH SPECIALTIES IN SPATIAL AND ECONOMIC ANALYSIS  RESPECTIVELY  WILL LEAD A PROJECT TO EVALUATE THE POSSIBILITY OF USING REMOTELY-SENSED INDICATORS TO EFFECTIVELY SHIELD FARMERS FROM RISKS OF ADOPTING HIGHER VALUE CROPS VIA THEIR USE IN AN INDEXED INSURANCE AND/OR DROUGHT RELIEF PROGRAM. ACHIEVING THIS OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE WILL INVOLVE THREE MAIN TASKS: 1. DETECTING THE EXTENT OF OLIVE CROPPING SYSTEMS AND EVALUATING THE DEGREE OF CONVERSION FROM CEREAL CROPS TO OLIVES. 2. EVALUATING SOCIOECONOMIC CONDITIONS AND RISK MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES IN TWO STUDY AREAS OF MOROCCO. THIS STEP WILL FIRST INVOLVE EXPERT ELICITATION TO GROUND THE ANALYSIS IN THE REALITIES AND PERCEIVED RISKS IN THE SUPPLY CHAIN  AND WILL BE FOLLOWED BY A SERIES OF STRATIFIED SURVEYS AMONG AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS IN TWO OLIVE PRODUCING REGIONS OF MOROCCO WHOSE AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS VARY. 3. INTEGRATING DATA ON SOCIOECONOMIC CONDITIONS WITH REMOTELY SENSED ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES TO EVALUATE THE CORRESPONDENCE OF A REMOTELY-SENSED TRIGGER OF FARMER LOSSES DUE TO ADVERSE CONDITIONS SUCH AS DROUGHT. PERENNIAL CROPS ARE EMBLEMATIC OF THE POSSIBILITY TO ADOPT HIGHER VALUE CROPPING SYSTEMS THAT ARE OTHERWISE TOO RISKY FOR MANY FARMERS TO TAKE ON WITHOUT INSURANCE. EVEN IF THEY ARE DROUGHT-RESISTANT  PERENNIALS ARE MUCH MORE COSTLY THAN MANY ANNUAL CROPS AND INVOLVE A LONG PERIOD BEFORE THEY HAVE ECONOMICALLY-HARVESTABLE FRUITS. DROUGHT CAN THEREFORE AMPLIFY RISK EXPOSURE FOR FARMERS WHEN THE FARMERS FACE HIGHER ABSOLUTE LOSSES RELATIVE TO THEIR POTENTIAL. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF PERENNIALS  MOST STUDIES EVALUATING INDEXED PRODUCTS FOR AGRICULTURE FOCUS ON ANNUAL CROPPING SYSTEMS OR BROAD INDICATORS OF DROUGHT STRESS RATHER THAN THE PARTICULARS OF HIGH VALUE  LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS. THREE SENIOR COLLABORATORS FROM UC DAVIS  UMN  AND THE NATIONAL SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE IN MEKNES  MOROCCO  WITH SIGNIFICANT ON-THE GROUND EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL EXPERTISE IN AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS AND AGRONOMY WILL ADVISE THE PROJECT TO ENSURE ALIGNMENT WITH THE REALITIES OF MOROCCO S ENVIRONMENT AND POLICY CONTEXT. Award or Action Description: THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES THE WEATHER AND CLIMATE THEMATIC SERVICE AREA OF THE A.35 SERVIR APPLIED SCIENCES TEAM (AST) SOLICITATION  WITH A SPECIFIC FOCUS ON SERVIR-HINDU KUSH HIMALAYA (HKH) REGION. AIR POLLUTION IN THE HKH REGION OF SOUTH-CENTRAL ASIA IS A SEVERE ISSUE  AS INCREASES IN EMISSIONS AND POLLUTANT LEVELS OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES HAVE DEGRADED AIR QUALITY (AQ) ACROSS THE REGION  WHICH POSES MAJOR THREATS TO THE ECOSYSTEM  HUMAN HEALTH  CLIMATE  AND AGRICULTURE. A DIVERSITY OF ANTHROPOGENIC AND NATURAL EMISSION SOURCES INCLUDING TRANSPORTATION  POWER PLANTS  INDUSTRIES  OPEN BIOMASS BURNING OF CROP RESIDUE  FOREST FIRES  COOKING AND HEATING FIRES  AND DUST STORMS CAN CONTRIBUTE TO THE ELEVATED POLLUTION LEVELS IN HKH. TRANSBOUNDARY POLLUTION IS A MAJOR CONCERN IN THE REGION  AS HIGH EMISSIONS FROM REGIONAL SOURCES SUCH AS FIRES CAN LEAD TO COMPLEX INFLUENCES ON LOCAL AQ. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO BUILD A FULLY CUSTOMIZED AND SUSTAINABLE AQ TOOLKIT FOR ADVANCING AQ MONITORING  FORECASTING  AND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS IN THE HKH FOCUS COUNTRIES. APPLICATION OF OUR ENHANCED AQ TOOLKIT WILL AID IN CHARACTERIZING AND QUANTIFYING DIURNALLY-VARYING SOURCE EMISSIONS AND ATTRIBUTIONS ON THE AQ STATE  PROVIDING CRITICAL INFORMATION TO THE SERVIRHKH HUB AND PARTNER AGENCIES ON TRANSBOUNDARY POLLUTION AND LOCAL-SCALE AQ ISSUES IN THE REGION. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT ARE AS FOLLOWS: (1) DEVELOP CUTTING-EDGE ALGORITHMS AND MACHINE LEARNING (ML) TECHNIQUES FROM SATELLITE DATA TO DELIVER NEAR REAL-TIME PRODUCTS AND TOOLS WITH ADVANCED PRECISION AND DETAIL ON EMISSIONS  TRANSBOUNDARY POLLUTANTS  AND LOCAL-SCALE AQ (2) IMPLEMENT NEWLY CUSTOMIZED MODEL SOLUTIONS WITH UPDATED EMISSION INVENTORIES AND ASSIMILATION PROCEDURES FOR IMPROVING AQ FORECASTS AND DECISION-MAKING ACTIVITIES (3) ACTIVELY ENGAGE WITH THE SERVIR-HKH HUB AND PARTNERS IN THE REGION THROUGH WORKSHOPS AND TRAINING TO TAILOR NEW PRODUCT SOLUTIONS/TOOLS TO SPECIFIC STAKEHOLDER NEEDS IN EACH HKH FOCUS COUNTRY  MAXIMIZING THE APPLICATION IMPACT AND SUSTAINABILITY OF OUR AQ TOOLKIT. OUR ML ALGORITHMS WILL UTILIZE SPECTRAL  SPATIAL  AND TEMPORAL INFORMATION FROM DIFFERENT BAND COMBINATIONS ON NEW-GENERATION GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITE SENSORS TO ACCURATELY CLASSIFY DUST AND SMOKE IN THE HKH REGION. THE DUST AND SMOKE CLASSIFICATIONS WILL BE USED TO DEVELOP AN ENHANCED AEROSOL OPTICAL DEPTH (AOD) PRODUCT AND SURFACE-LEVEL PARTICULATE MATTER ESTIMATES FOR THE REGION. WE WILL ALSO OPERATIONALIZE A THRESHOLD-BASED APPROACH USING GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITE DATA TO PROVIDE FIRE HOT SPOT LOCATIONS THROUGHOUT THE DAYTIME AND NIGHTTIME. THE AOD AND FIRE DETECTION PRODUCTS WILL BE USED AS INPUT INTO A HIGH-RESOLUTION WEATHER RESEARCH AND FORECASTING MODEL WITH CHEMISTRY (WRF-CHEM) CONFIGURATION OVER THE REGION. THE OPERATIONAL WRF-CHEM MODEL WILL ALSO BE UPDATED WITH A NEW ANTHROPOGENIC EMISSIONS INVENTORY BASED ON A SATELLITE-BASED ADJUSTMENT METHOD. LASTLY  THE FIRE DETECTION LOCATIONS  DUST CLASSIFICATIONS  AND AEROSOL LAYER HEIGHT PRODUCTS WILL BE USED TO INITIALIZE AN AUTOMATED HYSPLIT DISPERSION FORECASTING SYSTEM OVER HKH FOR RAPIDLY WARNING THE PUBLIC OF AQ EXCEEDANCES RELATED TO DUST AND SMOKE EPISODES. TO TAILOR OUR AQ PRODUCTS TO STAKEHOLDER NEEDS IN HKH  WE WILL ACTIVELY ENGAGE THE COMMUNITY THROUGH WORKSHOPS AND CUSTOMIZED TRAININGS OVER THE COURSE OF THE PROJECT  SUPPORTING LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF OUR PRODUCTS. WE AIM TO ACHIEVE AN APPLICATIONS READINESS LEVEL OF 8  APPLICATION SYSTEM COMPLETED AND QUALIFIED BY THE REGIONAL PARTNERS THROUGH TESTING AND DEMONSTRATION IN TARGETED DECISION-MAKING ACTIVITIES. Award or Action Description: SCIENCE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDINGS MADE BY PARKER SOLAR PROBE (PSP) IS THE LARGE NUMBER OF MAGNETIC SWITCHBACKS (SWITCHBACKS FOR SHORT) IN THE NEAR-SUN SPACE. SWITCHBACKS  WITH TYPICAL TIME SCALES OF MINUTES TO TENS OF MINUTES  ARE LOCAL POLARITY-REVERSALS OF THE (RADIAL) MAGNETIC FIELD AND ARE TYPICALLY HIGHLY ALFV NIC  WITH CORRELATIONS BETWEEN VELOCITY AND MAGNETIC FIELD CORRESPONDING TO LARGE-AMPLITUDE OUTWARD-PROPAGATING ALFV N WAVES. MANY OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES SUGGEST THAT SWITCHBACKS PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE EVOLUTION OF SOLAR WIND. EVIDENCE OF MAGNETIC RECONNECTION AND WAVE ACTIVITIES WAS FOUND AT THE BOUNDARIES OF SWITCHBACKS  AND THESE PROCESSES MAY FACILITATE THE ENERGY DISSIPATION IN THE SWITCHBACKS. SIMULATIONS SHOW THAT THE SWITCHBACKS CAN BE DESTROYED BY PARAMETRIC DECAY  RELEASING ENERGY TO THE BACKGROUND PLASMA. THUS  SWITCHBACKS MAY CONTRIBUTE SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE HEATING AND ACCELERATION OF THE SOLAR WIND. HOWEVER  HOW AND WHERE THE SWITCHBACKS ARE GENERATED IS STILL A MYSTERY  AND A QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THEIR INFLUENCES ON THE BACKGROUND SOLAR WIND IS STILL NEEDED. THE APPEARANCE AND AMPLITUDE OF SWITCHBACKS ARE USUALLY MODULATED BY A LARGE TIME SCALE  TYPICALLY SEVERAL HOURS  SO THAT THE SWITCHBACKS APPEAR IN PATCHES. THESE PATCHES ARE BELIEVED TO BE REMNANTS OF SPATIAL AND/OR TEMPORAL EFFECTS IN THE CORONAL SOURCE REGION OF THE WIND  SO THAT STUDYING THE PATCHES MAY HELP TO UNDERSTAND THE ORIGINS OF SWITCHBACKS. THUS  WE PROPOSE TO ANALYZE IN-SITU SATELLITE MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND REMOTE-SENSING OBSERVATIONS OF THE SUN IN ORDER TO ANSWER THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS: (1) HOW DO THE PROPERTIES OF SWITCHBACKS EVOLVE IN THE SOLAR WIND? WHAT CAN WE LEARN ABOUT THE GENERATION MECHANISMS OF THE SWITCHBACKS FROM THEIR PROPERTIES? (2) HOW MUCH DO THE SWITCHBACKS CONTRIBUTE TO THE ACCELERATION AND HEATING OF THE SOLAR WIND? (3) WHAT IS THE ORIGIN OF THE SWITCHBACK PATCHES? ARE THEY RELATED TO CERTAIN SPATIAL STRUCTURES OR TEMPORAL PROCESSES IN THE SOLAR CORONA? METHODOLOGY: WE WILL COMBINE IN-SITU MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND REMOTE SENSING MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR ATMOSPHERE. WE WILL USE INSITU DATA FROM PSP  SOLAR ORBITER AND WIND TO IDENTIFY SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES IN THE SOLAR WIND. THEN WE WILL CONDUCT ANALYSES OF THE PROPERTIES OF SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES  INCLUDING HOW THEY EVOLVE AS THE SOLAR WIND PROPAGATES. WE WILL SELECT TIME INTERVALS WHEN PSP IS GOING THROUGH FAST RADIAL SCAN AND ESTIMATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE SWITCHBACKS TO THE ACCELERATION AND HEATING OF THE SOLAR WIND. THE REMOTE SENSING DATA WILL BE FROM HELIOSEISMIC AND MAGNETIC IMAGER (HMI) AND ATMOSPHERIC IMAGING ASSEMBLY (AIA) ONBOARD SOLAR DYNAMICS OBSERVATORY (SDO). WE WILL USE THE REMOTE SENSING DATA  COMBINED WITH TECHNIQUES SUCH AS THE POTENTIAL-FIELD-SOURCE-SURFACE MODEL  TO IDENTIFY SOURCE REGIONS OF THE SOLAR WIND STREAMS MEASURED IN-SITU BY PSP AND OTHER SATELLITES. RELEVANCE: KNOWLEDGE OF THE PROPERTIES AND ORIGINS OF MAGNETIC SWITCHBACKS WILL GREATLY IMPROVE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ORIGINS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND HOW THE SOLAR WIND IS ACCELERATED AND HEATED. THUS  IT IS DIRECTLY RELATED TO ONE OF THE HELIOPHYSICS OVERARCHING GOALS:  EXPLORE AND CHARACTERIZE THE PHYSICAL PROCESSES IN THE SPACE ENVIRONMENT FROM THE SUN TO THE HELIOPAUSE AND THROUGHOUT THE UNIVERSE.  BESIDES  GENERATION OF THE SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES IS A RESULT OF THE SUN S ACTIVITY  SO THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO THE HELIOPHYSICS OVERARCHING GOAL:  ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE SUN S ACTIVITY.  FURTHERMORE  AS THE SWITCHBACKS MAY PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN HEATING AND ACCELERATING THE SOLAR WIND AS WELL AS ENERGIZING PARTICLES  THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL HELP US DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND CAPABILITY TO DETECT AND PREDICT EXTREME CONDITIONS IN SPACE TO PROTECT LIFE AND SOCIETY AND TO SAFEGUARD HUMAN AND ROBOTIC EXPLORERS BEYOND EARTH.

NASA HAS SELECTED A FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND EARTH SCIENCE MISSION THAT WILL EXTEND OUR NATION'S LEAD IN MEASURING KEY GREENHOUSE GASES AND VEGETATION HEALTH FROM SPACE TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF EARTH'S NATURAL EXCHANGES OF CARBON BETWEEN THE LAND, ATMOSPHERE AND OCEAN. THE MISSION WAS COMPETITIVELY SELECTED FROM 15 PROPOSALS SUBMITTED TO THE AGENCY'S SECOND EARTH VENTURE - MISSION ANNOUNCEMENT OF OPPORTUNITY FOR SMALL ORBITAL INVESTIGATIONS OF THE EARTH SYSTEM.  THE PRIMARY GOALS OF THE GEOCARB MISSION ARE TO MONITOR PLANT HEALTH AND VEGETATION STRESS THROUGHOUT THE AMERICAS, TO PROBE, IN UNPRECEDENTED DETAIL, THE NATURAL SOURCES, SINKS AND EXCHANGE PROCESSES THAT CONTROL CARBON DIOXIDE, CARBON MONOXIDE AND METHANE IN THE ATMOSPHERE, AND TO PROVIDE OBSERVATIONS AND DEMONSTRATE METHODS TO REALIZE A TRANSFORMATIONAL ADVANCE IN THE SCIENTIFIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE GLOBAL CARBON CYCLE. THE INSTRUMENT WILL ALSO MEASURE SOLAR-INDUCED FLUORESCENCE (SIF), WHICH PROVIDES DIRECT INFORMATION ABOUT PHOTOSYNTHESIS.  THE CONTRACTOR AND ITS TEAM MEMBERS WILL PERFORM THE FULL NASA LIFE CYCLE FORMULATION AND IMPLEMENTATION PHASES A THROUGH F. THE GEOCARB PROPOSAL WAS SELECTED UNDER THE NASA ANNOUNCEMENT OF OPPORTUNITY NNH15ZDA011O FOR THE EARTH VENTURE MISSION - 2 ELEMENT OF THE EARTH SYSTEM SCIENCE PATHFINDER PROGRAM OFFICES EARTH VENTURE LINE.

Award or Action Description: CLAY MINERALS PRESENT A CONUNDRUM ON MARS- WHILE WE OBSERVE RELATIVELY THICK LAYERS OF CLAY MINERALS AND OTHER SECONDARY MINERALS WHICH ARE TYPICALLY FORMED THROUGH AQUEOUS PROCESSES ON EARTH  CLIMATE MODELS PREDICT COLD CONDITIONS ON EARLY MARS THAT PRECLUDE LONG-TERM STABILITY OF FRESH WATER ON THE SURFACE. ADDING SALT DECREASES THE FREEZING POINT OF WATER  ALLOWING LONG-TERM STABILITY OF LIQUID WATER AT COLDER TEMPERATURES AND LOWER PRESSURES. SALTS ALSO ALLOW FOR THIN FILMS OF WATER AT MINERAL SURFACES. PREVIOUS EXPERIMENTS CONDUCTED BY OUR RESEARCH GROUP DEMONSTRATE THAT MINERAL-BRINE INTERACTIONS CAN PRODUCE CLAY MINERALS WITHIN WEEKS OF REACTION WITH PRIMARY ROCK-FORMING SILICATES. HERE WE AIM TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE THE MINERALOGY AND ABUNDANCE OF CLAY MINERAL PHASES PRODUCED WHEN PRIMARY SILICATE MINERALS REACT WITH HIGH SALINITY BRINES. IN ADDITION  WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE CLAY ALTERATION IN HIGH SALINITY BRINES TO FURTHER UNDERSTAND THE POTENTIAL EFFECTS OF EVAPORATING/FREEZING SURFACE WATERS AS WELL AS HIGH DENSITY DIAGENETIC FLUIDS ON CLAY MINERALOGY AND CHEMISTRY. OUR PREVIOUS MINERAL-BRINE DISSOLUTION EXPERIMENTS WERE DESIGNED TO MEASURE PRIMARY MINERAL WEATHERING RATES IN HIGH SALINITY FLUIDS. WHILE SECONDARY CLAY MINERALS WERE OBSERVED AT THE MICRON SCALE VIA SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (SEM) AND RAMAN SPECTROSCOPY  THEY PROVED DIFFICULT TO FULLY ANALYZE USING X-RAY DIFFRACTION (XRD) METHODS DUE TO THEIR LIMITED ABUNDANCE. HERE  WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT LONGER-TERM BRINE WEATHERING EXPERIMENTS USING SIGNIFICANTLY LARGER QUANTITIES OF REACTANTS  INCLUDING PYROXENE  OLIVINE  PLAGIOCLASE FELDSPAR  MAFIC SILICATE GLASS  AND BASALT IN ORDER TO PRODUCE SUFFICIENT REACTION PRODUCTS NEEDED TO CHARACTERIZE THE SECONDARY MINERALS USING A WIDE RANGE OF ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES. FURTHERMORE  WE WILL EXPLORE THE ROLE OF BRINE CHEMISTRY ON CLAY DIAGENESIS AND WEATHERING BY REACTING CLAY MINERALS WITH THE BRINES. MINERAL AND ROCK SAMPLES WILL BE REACTED WITH NEAR-SATURATED BRINES AND 1:10 DILUTED SOLUTIONS OF NACL  NA2SO4  NACLO4  CACL2  MGCL2  MGSO4  AND NH4CL OVER 6 MONTHS  THEN FILTERED TO COLLECT THE SOLID AND LIQUID REACTION PRODUCTS. ADDITIONAL HIGH TEMPERATURE (350K FOR 50 DAYS) AND LOW TEMPERATURE EXPERIMENTS (250K FOR 450 DAYS) WILL BE CONDUCTED WITH BASALT AND MAFIC GLASS. THE CLAY-SIZED FRACTION WILL BE SEPARATED VIA WET SIEVING AND CENTRIFUGE TECHNIQUES. SIMILAR EXPERIMENTS WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED USING CLAY STANDARDS (KAOLINITE  NONTRONITE  SMECTITE  CHLORITE). THE MINERALOGY OF THE REACTION PRODUCTS WILL BE DETERMINED USING X-RAY DIFFRACTION OF BOTH RANDOM POWDERS AND ORIENTED CLAY MOUNTS (WITH AND WITHOUT HEAT AND GLYCOL TREATMENTS)  AS WELL AS RAMAN SPECTROSCOPY. BULK CHEMISTRY OF THE CLAY-SIZED FRACTION WILL BE DETERMINED VIA ICP OPTICAL EMISSION SPECTROSCOPY ANALYSIS OF DIGESTIONS. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE REACTION PRODUCT MINERALOGY  MORPHOLOGY  CHEMISTRY AND TEXTURAL RELATIONSHIPS USING BOTH SCANNING AND TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF POTENTIAL MINERAL-BRINE INTERACTIONS ON MARS AND OTHER SALTY WORLDS  INCLUDING CERES  EUROPA  AND ENCELADUS AND WILL PROVIDE RICHER CONTEXT FOR INTERPRETING MINERAL ASSEMBLAGES AND SEDIMENTARY ROCKS  INCLUDING CLAY MINERALS  OBSERVED ON THESE BODIES. THUS  THIS WORK IS RELEVANT TO THE SSW PROGRAM AS IT INVESTIGATES  GEOCHEMICAL PROCESSES OCCURRING ON PLANETARY BODIES  SATELLITES  AND OTHER MINOR BODIES  AND SEEKS TO  INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE FUNDAMENTAL PROCESSES AT WORK BY CHARACTERIZING AND UNDERSTANDING  THE CHEMICAL  MINERALOGICAL  AND PHYSICAL FEATURES OF PLANETARY SURFACES (SUCH AS GEOLOGIC FORMATIONS AND IMPACT CRATERS) AND FLUID INVENTORIES THAT INTERACT WITH THE SURFACE (INCLUDING HYDROSPHERES  CRYOSPHERES  ATMOSPHERES  AND OTHER VOLATILE RESERVOIRS).  AND DEVELOPS  THEORETICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL BASES FOR UNDERSTANDING THESE FEATURES IN THE CONTEXT OF THE VARYING CONDITIONS THROUGH TIME AFTER FORMATION.
